plugin_lol_description: This match's 10 players' history and weak spots, anyone's match history, the summoner spells the enemy used; champion strength, counters, builds and ARAM Mayhem augments
plugin_lol_source_client_desc: Reads League of Legends' local client and in-game APIs (read-only, nothing is changed) to look up the history of this match's players, point out the enemy's weak spot, and track the summoner spells the enemy used; the game hub also uses it to know phases like champion select, loading and in match, and in-game events.
plugin_lol_source_client_risk: On the Chinese (Tencent) servers this kind of feature may break Tencent's user agreement; tools like LeagueAkari have reports of bans and chat mutes, and Riot restricts third-party cooldown timers. Whether to use it is your call.
plugin_lol_settings_intro: {companion} needs the switches below to read this match's data. Changes apply right away; {companion}'s tool list follows from the next conversation.
plugin_lol_game_section_desc: Match history, weak spots and summoner spells for this game come from the League of Legends plugin.
plugin_lol_game_section_open: Open the League of Legends plugin
plugin_lol_events_off: The League of Legends plugin's "Read client data" is off: only the generic events arrive (start, close, window switches, match start and end), not phases like champion select or loading, nor in-game events.
plugin_lol_push_opening_when: During loading, once all 10 players' stats are in (at most 20 seconds)
plugin_lol_push_opening_what: Posts a card with both teams' stats and leaves her a short note
plugin_lol_push_summary_when: At the end of the match, once the result is in
plugin_lol_push_summary_what: Posts a match summary card (match details) and leaves her a short note
plugin_lol_game_section_plugin_off: The League of Legends plugin is off: turn it on first under Plugins in the left sidebar.
plugin_lol_search_placeholder: Name#tag, or a champion or player in this match
plugin_lol_card_more: {count} more games — open to see all
plugin_lol_source_stats_desc: Looks up League of Legends stats on the web (Chinese servers): Tencent 101 / Zhangmeng tier lists, counters, builds, runes, skill orders and the ARAM Mayhem champion ranking; czgreat/aramhex-data's ARAM Mayhem champion × augment win rates; Tencent's champion nicknames. Requested only on demand (when a page opens or she asks), never with your account.
plugin_lol_source_stats_risk: The data comes from unofficial Tencent and aramhex endpoints with no documentation that may change or stop at any time; aramhex data is CC BY-NC 4.0, which requires attribution and no commercial use (Kotone is free, and the pages credit the source).
plugin_lol_source_opgg_desc: Adds global data (champion builds and counter analysis) from OP.GG's official MCP, requested only when a champion page opens or she looks up a champion, cached for 24 hours; the page credits OP.GG with a link.
plugin_lol_source_opgg_risk: We asked OP.GG on your behalf whether Kotone may use it (github.com/opgginc/opgg-mcp/issues/26); it stays off by default until OP.GG agrees. The site's terms forbid automated scripts, so turning it on now is your own call.
plugin_lol_champion_search_placeholder: Champion name, title or nickname (Irelia, Yasuo)
plugin_lol_champion_empty: Enter a champion to see its strength, counters, builds and ARAM Mayhem augments.
plugin_lol_augments_note: Numbers are how many percentage points {champion}'s win rate with this augment is above its average (small samples are pulled toward the average).
plugin_lol_source_control_desc: Controls the League of Legends client the way LeagueAkari does: accepts matches automatically and picks / bans champions automatically in the order you set; she accepts a match or picks / bans a champion for you only when you say so. Reads and writes go only through the client's own local API — no game memory reading, no injection. "Read client data" must be on too.
plugin_lol_source_control_risk: Players on other servers were permanently banned after using auto-accept and auto-pick (LeagueAkari's github.com/LeagueAkari/LeagueAkari/issues/523), and on the Chinese servers it may break Tencent's user agreement. Off by default; turning it on means you accept this risk yourself.
plugin_lol_source_chat_desc: In champion select and in the lobby, what you say with voice input and what she sends for you goes out through the client's own local chat API, with no key presses (the way LeagueAkari does it). Several lines go out as one message. It only sends when you speak, ask her to send, or a hotkey or automation you set up sends. "Read client data" must be on too.
plugin_lol_source_chat_risk: On the Chinese servers third-party tools may break Tencent's user agreement; messages sent through the API still go through Tencent's word filter and chat-ban rules (LeagueAkari users reported template words being filtered: github.com/LeagueAkari/LeagueAkari/issues/480; WeGame removed its editable one-key callouts: github.com/LeagueAkari/LeagueAkari/issues/524). Riot says the client API is not officially supported for third-party use (developer.riotgames.com/docs/lol). With it off, she won't send for you in champion select; your own voice input still types into the window in front.
plugin_lol_control_intro: Like LeagueAkari: accept matches automatically and pick / ban champions in the order you set. Changes apply right away.
plugin_lol_control_off: Turn on "Control the client" above first (read the ban-risk note); these preferences only apply while it's on.
plugin_lol_control_needs_client: "Read client data" is off: controlling the client needs to read it too, so turn that on first.
plugin_lol_control_accept_desc: Clicks "Accept" once a match is found; if you already accepted or declined, it does nothing.
plugin_lol_control_pick_desc: On your pick turn, takes the first champion from the top that can be picked (banned or taken ones are skipped).
plugin_lol_control_lock_desc: When off, it only shows the champion and you lock in yourself.
plugin_lol_control_ban_desc: On your ban turn, bans the first champion from the top that can be banned; already-banned champions and a teammate's wish are skipped.
plugin_lol_control_list_empty: No champions yet; search below to add some.
plugin_lol_control_add_placeholder: Search a champion to add (name or title)
plugin_lol_control_note: Follows LeagueAkari's rules: skips champions that are banned or taken, never bans a teammate's wish, and acts once per turn. Reads and writes go only through the client's own local API — no game memory reading, no injection.

plugin_lol_not_in_game: Not in a match right now. Once champ select starts, the players show up here.

plugin_lol_start_records: Records at the start of the match
plugin_lol_state_ambiguous: Several players match. Search with the full "name#tag".
plugin_lol_state_champ_select: Still in champ select. Once loading starts, all 10 players' records show up here.
plugin_lol_state_client_closed: The League of Legends client isn't open. This page updates once it is.
plugin_lol_state_disabled: Turn on this page's data switch in settings first (the risks are written there).
plugin_lol_state_error: Couldn't read it. Try Refresh in a moment.
plugin_lol_state_loading: The game is still loading. This page updates once you're in.
plugin_lol_state_not_found: Not found. Try another spelling (name#tag, champion name or nickname).
